title: C367 — Driver-side airbag connector
introduction:
The broad driver-side airbag title becomes more specific in the function descriptions: this reference concerns the seat-mounted front driver outboard airbag connection. I check that wording before using the drawing; “driver airbag” by itself is a fairly roomy label.

Use the identity table to establish which connector is documented, then match the drawing’s cavity labels to the pin-assignment rows. The positive and negative function markings distinguish the paired restraint circuits; they are not instructions to connect battery power or chassis ground. The pigtail table separately records the listed service assembly and engineering shell.

This is an identification and wiring-reading reference. It does not teach connector release, physical terminal-side or wire-side viewing direction, depowering, probing, diagnosis or replacement. Gauge conventions and the Size and Used codes remain undefined reference data. Understanding the map is useful; servicing a deployable restraint requires its own prescribed method.

items.name: Qualified personnel and the selected service procedure
items.detail: Pyrotechnic-component service is restricted to qualified personnel. Any work beyond reading this reference requires the applicable restraint procedure’s depowering, handling, equipment and restoration sequence; this page supplies none of those operations.

items.name: Use restraint-specific diagnosis
items.detail: Do not substitute a generic jumper or resistance test. Record fault information and use the restraint-specific diagnostic path. An apparently attached connector alone does not establish that its connector-position-assurance tab and shorting arrangement are correctly configured.

edits.why: The drawing places a circular cavity area at the right of an elongated housing, with the cavity labels stacked vertically. I use the asymmetric details inside the circular area to keep the pictured layout recognizable. Their shape alone does not establish a release movement or verify the connector’s locking state.

Read across each cavity row so its circuit identifier, color, gauge and signed function description stay together. The seat-mounted front driver outboard wording is the component qualifier that matters here. The signed descriptions distinguish the circuit pair without establishing a safe test connection, a normal reading or a fault conclusion.

Match the identity table’s Kit List entry to Number in the pigtail table, then distinguish the listed Service Part from its Engineering Shell. A pigtail listing identifies a service assembly; it does not prescribe a repair technique. Keep the terminal and material entries as written rather than treating either as an instruction for individual-terminal repair.
